g: (sports, historical, uncountable) A ceremonial ball game once played by the Aztecs; evolved into the ulama game.
The object of tlachtli was to keep the rubber ball from touching the ground while trying to push it to the opponent's endline.
(sports, historical, countable) The high-walled court in which this game was played.
(historical) one-eighth of a Mexican real (issued until 1897)
A Mexican dish consisting of a fried and stuffed masa cake.
(mineralogy) An orthorhombic mineral containing chlorine, copper, hydrogen, oxygen, tellurium, and zinc.
(mineralogy) A monoclinic mineral containing calcium, copper, hydrogen, lead, oxygen, sulfur, and tellurium.
(physics, rare) A scalar field that acts as torsion potential.

A native or inhabitant of Tlaxcala.
